parts.title: Notices and messages

notices: CAREERS FAIR: Meet employers from twenty local companies in the school hall on Friday from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Bring a copy of your CV if you have one.
WORK EXPERIENCE: Students in Year 10 will spend two weeks in a workplace in June. Forms must be returned to Mrs Ortega by Friday 12 May.

parts.title: A year off
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I finished school, everyone expected me to go straight to university. Instead, I decided to take a year off. My parents were worried at first, and my teacher told me that I would forget everything I had learnt. But I wanted to see the world before I chose a career.

For the first four months, I worked in a supermarket to save money. It was not very exciting, and my back hurt from lifting boxes, but I knew it was only for a short time. In January, I flew to Peru, where I spent six months teaching English in a small village school.

The children were wonderful. They arrived early every morning, and they listened carefully to every word I said. After the lessons, we often played football on a dusty field. I learnt Spanish from them far faster than I could have done from a book, and I made friends who I still write to.

When I came home, I felt like a different person. I was more confident, and I knew exactly what I wanted to study: education. Looking back, I do not regret the year for one minute. It was the best decision I have ever made.

Because he could not choose a university
Because he failed his final exams
To see the world before choosing a career
questions.explanation: He wanted to see the world before choosing a career.

questions.explanation: He worked there to save money.

options: He built houses for a charity
He worked on a farm for a family
He taught English in a village school
He studied Spanish in a language school
questions.explanation: He spent six months teaching English.

questions.explanation: He learnt it from the children.

He wishes he had saved more
He is very glad that he did it
questions.explanation: He does not regret it and calls it the best decision.

parts.title: Starting your first job
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Starting your first job can be exciting and a little frightening at the same time. [1] Everything is new, from the people you meet to the rules you must follow, so it is normal to feel nervous.

On your first day, arrive a little early. [2] Smile, introduce yourself and try to remember people's names, even if it is difficult at first.

Do not be afraid to ask questions. [3] Your colleagues would much prefer that you ask than make a mistake that nobody notices until later.

It is also important to be reliable. [4] If you say that you will finish something by Friday, make sure that you do. Over time, people will learn to trust you. [5] Finally, remember that everybody makes mistakes when they start, and what matters is that you learn from them.
sentences: Nobody expects you to know everything immediately.
This means that people can depend on you.
You may need to travel a long way to get there.
You will probably get your first pay at the end of the month.
This is the moment when you make your first impression.
Then they will start to give you more interesting work.
Many young people find their first job through a friend.
Many people feel this way before the first morning arrives.

gaps.explanation: Feeling this way before the first morning leads to why everything is new.
Arriving early is when you make a first impression, then you smile and introduce yourself.
Nobody expects you to know everything, so do not be afraid to ask questions.
Being reliable means that people can depend on you; the Friday example follows.
When people trust you, they start to give you more interesting work.

parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Choosing a job is one of the most important decisions in life. Many young people feel pressure to decide [1] they are still at school, but it is fine to change your mind. A good way to start is to think about what you enjoy doing most. Do you like working [2] people, or do you prefer to work alone? Are you good [3] solving problems? You can also talk to adults who do jobs that interest you. Ask them what they like [4] their work and what they find difficult. Remember that most people have several different jobs in [5] lives, so you do not need to be perfect from the start. The most important thing is to find something that makes [6] happy.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Hello, Mrs Doyle? It’s Justin, Ben’s dad. What time should Ben go to the careers fair on Friday?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: It’s open all day. The morning is the busiest, because the whole school goes then, and you can hardly talk to anybody. There is a talk at three o’clock, but the engineers leave by two. Ben is interested in engineering, isn’t he?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, he is.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Then I’d go straight after lunch, around one. There are fewer students, and all the engineers are there.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Great, I’ll tell him. Does he need to take anything with him?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Just a notebook and a pen. They give out free bags and plenty of leaflets.

question.prompt: When should the boy go to the careers fair?
question.explanation: The morning is too crowded and the talk at three comes after the engineers leave; she says to go straight after lunch.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: How was the interview, Eli?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Better than I thought. I had prepared for questions about my school marks, but they hardly mentioned them. They asked about my last job at the supermarket for a few minutes, but mostly they wanted to know what I do in my free time. I talked about football and my guitar for ten minutes.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s a surprise. Did they like it?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I think so. They kept smiling and asking more questions.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Then I hope you get the job. When will they tell you?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Next Friday, they said.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Then try not to think about it until then.

question.prompt: What did the interviewers mostly ask about?
question.explanation: He prepared for the school marks and they asked briefly about the supermarket, but they mostly asked about football and the guitar.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: How much are you going to get for the Saturday job at the café, Adele?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Eight pounds an hour. I start at eight in the morning and finish at four, and I get a free lunch.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: That’s better than my job last summer. I got forty for the whole day at the shop.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Really? Then I’m lucky. The manager says that I may work more hours in the holidays too.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Not bad at all. You’ll be rich by Christmas. Is it hard work, or can you sit down sometimes?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: It’s hard, but the customers are friendly, and I like the other girls.

question.prompt: How much will she earn each Saturday?
question.explanation: She earns eight pounds an hour and works from eight to four, which is eight hours, so she gets more than the forty that Felix earned.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Is your son still planning to be a vet, Dean?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, Leo told me yesterday that he definitely wants it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Because of you? You work with animals, don’t you?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’m a farmer, and my wife and I would like him to take over the farm one day, but he says no.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Ah, so he loves being outdoors?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Not really, he hates the rain. What changed him was our dog’s illness last year, when the vet saved her. Leo said he wants to be the one who makes sick animals better.

question.prompt: Why does the boy want to be a vet?
options: He wants to help ill animals
question.explanation: His parents want him to take over the farm and he hates the rain; he was moved when a vet saved the family’s dog.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Have you decided what to do after school, Jolene?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I’ve been accepted at university, but I’m not starting this September. Many of my friends are going straight away, though.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: And you’re going travelling, aren’t you?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Yes, I want to go to Asia for three months, but that isn’t the first thing. Before that I need to earn money, so I’ll work at my uncle’s shop for a year. Then I’ll go travelling, and when I come back I’ll start my course.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: That sounds like a good plan.

question.prompt: What will the woman do first?
question.explanation: She will not start university now and travelling comes later; before that she needs money, so she will work at her uncle’s shop for a year.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: How’s the new job, Bruce?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Great, honestly. The salary is better than at the last place, so I can’t complain. And the office is open-plan, but people are quiet.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: So what’s wrong? You look tired.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: It’s the journey. It takes an hour and a half each way, with two trains and a bus. I leave at six and get home at eight.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s awful. Can’t you work from home?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Two days a week, starting next month. I can’t wait. I’ll have time to cook dinner for once, and maybe I’ll even start running again.

question.prompt: What does the man dislike about his job?
question.explanation: The pay is better and the office is quiet; he is tired because the journey to work takes an hour and a half each way.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: How was Kenji’s work experience at the hotel, Dahlia?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: He loved it. At first he was sad, because his friends were together in an office and he was alone. And the lunch break was only twenty minutes! But what changed everything was the guests. People came from Spain, Japan and Brazil, and every day he practised his English and learnt words in other languages.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: That sounds great.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: He wants to do it again next summer, and he has already asked the manager if there is a job for him. I think he may study languages now.

question.prompt: What did the boy like about his work experience?
question.explanation: He was alone and the lunch break was short; he enjoyed the guests from Spain, Japan and Brazil and practising languages with them.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Big day tomorrow, Jacob. Are you ready for the interview?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’ve practised answers for a week, so I know what to say. But my stomach has been strange all day.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: You’ll be fine. You always say you’ll fail, and then you do well.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’m not saying I’ll fail. I’m not saying I’ll get it either. It’s a great company, and honestly I can’t wait to meet them. I just wish it were over.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Take a deep breath and enjoy it. Go to bed early, and send me a message when it is finished.

Worried that he is not ready
Nervous but looking forward to it
question.explanation: He has practised, so he is not unprepared, and he does not promise success; he is nervous but can’t wait to meet the company.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I heard you’re leaving the bank, Patrick. Is it the money?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No, I earn well, and my colleagues are lovely. I’ll miss them. But I spend all day moving numbers, and at the end I never feel I’ve done anything.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: So what will you do?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’m training to be a nurse. It’s a big change at forty-five, and half the money, but I want to go home feeling that I helped someone.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That sounds brave. What does your family think? Your wife must be worried about the money.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: She is, a little, but she supports me, and we have saved enough for two years.

question.prompt: Why is Patrick leaving the bank?
options: He wants to feel that he helps people
He is unhappy with his salary
He has problems with his colleagues
question.explanation: He says the money and colleagues are fine; he wants a job where he goes home feeling that he helped someone.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Julius, did the company phone?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes. They gave the job to somebody else.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Oh, I’m so sorry. You must be angry.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Funny, but no. They were polite, and they gave me feedback. And to be honest, after the second interview I wasn’t sure I wanted to travel an hour every day. I think I’m a little relieved. My family knows already, and they were fine about it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Then I’m glad. There will be other jobs, and next time you will know what they ask in the interview.

question.prompt: How does Julius feel about not getting the job?
options: Embarrassed in front of his family
question.explanation: He is not angry because they were polite, and the family was fine about it; he says that he is a little relieved.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: How’s the new job, Jacinta? And the new manager? My friends say he’s terrible.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Strict? Not at all. People said he was cold, but he’s actually warm. The first week was a bit chaotic, I couldn’t find anything in the shared folder, but that’s normal. The best thing is that he trusts me. He says, you decide how to do it, and I can start early or work from home.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: That sounds ideal. I wish my boss was like that.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: It is. I feel really lucky.

question.prompt: What does Jacinta think of her new manager?
options: He lets her decide for herself
question.explanation: He is not strict and the chaos was only the first week; the best thing is that he trusts her and says that she decides how to do it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Are you looking for a summer job, Milo?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, but the pay is terrible. Last year I got five pounds an hour at the ice-cream stand.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Same for me at the cinema. It’s not much, but I don’t mind. And it was easy to get, I just asked the manager.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Lucky you, it took me weeks. But I learnt a lot, how to deal with angry customers, how to work in a team, how to arrive on time.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Exactly! That helped me at school too.

question.prompt: What do Ellie and Milo agree about summer jobs?
options: They pay better than people say
question.explanation: Only Ellie found a job easily and both say that the pay is low; they agree on what they learnt, like teamwork and arriving on time.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I can’t decide between nursing and teaching, Larry. The university wants an answer by March.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Why not wait until next year? Lots of people take a year out.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I thought of that, but my parents wouldn’t be happy, and I don’t want to lose a year.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Then try the shorter course, to see.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: It doesn’t help. It only exists for teaching.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Honestly, I’d phone a nurse and a teacher and ask them what a normal day is like. That’s what I did, and it made my choice easy.

question.prompt: What does Larry advise Sienna to do?
options: Talk to people with different jobs
question.explanation: Waiting for a year would upset her parents and the short course only exists for teaching; he advises phoning a nurse and a teacher to ask about their days.

parts.title: A talk about work experience
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: hilary
turns.text: Good morning, Year Ten. Today I want to explain how work experience will work this summer. You will spend two weeks in a workplace, starting on the fifth of June. The letter that we sent home says the twelfth, but that is a mistake, so please tell your parents. Now, the place. You can choose almost anything, a shop, a vet’s, an office, but it must be easy to get to. Last year a boy chose a company forty kilometres away and spent three hours on trains every day. This year the rule is that your workplace must be within ten kilometres of your home. If you are a little further away, say twenty, we can talk about it, but I will probably say no. What should you wear? Many of you will think that jeans and trainers are fine. They aren’t. Some jobs are casual, but the first impression matters, so I want you to wear smart clothes, a shirt or a blouse and tidy shoes. If the company gives you a uniform, then of course wear it. What about food? Some companies will give you lunch in their canteen. It isn’t a rule, so bring a sandwich just in case. They will not pay for your travel, either. During the two weeks you will keep a diary, and afterwards you must write a short report. It should be about five hundred words. Last year some students wrote a thousand, and that is too long, because I have to read all of them. In the report, tell me what you did, what you learnt and whether you would like this kind of job. If you have questions, come and see me. My room is on the first floor. It is Room Twelve, next to the library. Don’t go to Room Fourteen, that’s the science lab. Thank you for listening, and good luck.

gaps.prompt: Placements begin on the ___ of June
gaps.explanation: The letter says the twelfth, but that is a mistake; the placements start on the fifth.

gaps.prompt: Your workplace must be no further than ___ kilometres from home
gaps.explanation: Last year’s boy travelled forty kilometres and twenty needs permission; the rule is within ten kilometres.

gaps.prompt: Students are asked to dress in ___ clothes
gaps.explanation: Jeans and trainers are not fine and some jobs are casual, but she wants smart clothes.

gaps.prompt: Some firms will give you a free ___
gaps.explanation: Some companies give lunch in their canteen, but they will not pay for travel.

gaps.prompt: After the placement, the report should have around ___ words
gaps.explanation: Last year some students wrote a thousand, which is too long; it should be about five hundred.

gaps.prompt: To see the teacher, go to Room ___
gaps.explanation: Her room is Room Twelve, next to the library; Room Fourteen is the science lab.

parts.title: A volunteer worker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: Ingrid, why did you decide to volunteer in Africa?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: People assume I had no choice, that I couldn’t find a job at home. In fact, I had two offers. And it wasn’t about language, because they speak English in the village, and I never learned the local one well. The truth is simple: after university I felt that my life was all about me, exams and money. I wanted to do something that was useful for other people.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What was your job in the village?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: I’m not a teacher, although the children asked me to join their lessons, and I worked on a farm for a few days at harvest time. But my main task was building a small clinic. I carried bricks, mixed cement and painted the walls. It took seven months, with about twenty people from the village.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What was the hardest part?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: The heat was awful in the afternoon, but we stopped work from twelve to three, so it was okay. The food was strange at first, but I loved it after a week. What really hurt was missing my family. I phoned my mother on Sundays, but the line was bad, and I cried a lot. Birthdays were the worst.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What did you learn there?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: I didn’t learn to drive a lorry, although I sat in one. I cooked a lot, but I had done that before. The main thing is patience. Nothing happens on time. The cement arrives a week late, it rains, and you can do nothing about it. Shouting doesn’t help. You wait, you smile, and you start again tomorrow.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: Have your plans changed?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: Yes, completely. I studied engineering, and I thought I would build bridges. Now I’m not so sure. A doctor visited the clinic every month, and I watched her work. I’m applying for medicine next year. It will take six years, but I’m ready. Art teacher? No, that was a childhood dream.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What advice would you give to somebody who wants to do the same?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: Don’t rush. Some people go as soon as they decide, and they end up in a place where the organisation doesn’t look after them. Money isn’t a problem, you need very little. But take time to check the project. Ask questions, talk to others who went. A good project is a wonderful thing, and a bad one is a disaster. I was lucky, and I would go again tomorrow if my family could come too.

questions.prompt: Why did Ingrid decide to go to Africa?
options: She could not find a job at home
She needed to learn a language
She wanted to do something useful
questions.explanation: She had two job offers and language was not the reason; she wanted to do something useful for other people.

questions.prompt: What was her main job in the village?
questions.explanation: The teaching was only joining lessons and the farm was a few days at harvest; her main task was building the clinic.

questions.prompt: What was the hardest part for Ingrid?
questions.explanation: They stopped work in the heat and she loved the food after a week; what really hurt was missing her family.

questions.prompt: What did Ingrid learn?
questions.explanation: She only sat in a lorry and had cooked before; the main thing she learnt is patience.

questions.prompt: How have her plans changed?
options: She now wants to study medicine
She now wants to be an engineer
She now wants to teach art
questions.explanation: Engineering was her old plan and art teacher was a childhood dream; she is now applying for medicine.

questions.prompt: What advice does she give?

parts.title: Getting to know you
parts.instructions: Answer each question in your own words. Aim to speak for 20-30 seconds.

questions.prompt: What job would you like to do in the future? Why?
Do you know anyone who has an interesting job?
What are you good at?
Would you like to work in your own country or abroad? Why?

parts.title: Describe a photograph
parts.instructions: Look at the photograph and speak for about one minute. Describe what you can see and say what the people might be feeling.
parts.prompt: Young people talking to employers at a careers fair.
